events.title: Benjamin Franklin Becomes the First Postmaster General
events.description: The Second Continental Congress appointed Benjamin Franklin to lead a postal system for the American colonies. The role put the famous printer, scientist and diplomat in charge of moving mail during the opening phase of the Revolutionary War.
events.significance: It created the foundation of what became the United States Postal Service, one of the country's oldest public institutions.

events.title: New York Ratifies the U.S. Constitution
events.description: After heated debate, New York's convention voted to ratify the Constitution and became the 11th state to join the Union. The vote was close and came after supporters promised that amendments protecting individual rights would be considered.
events.significance: New York's approval was essential to the new government's viability, given the state's size, wealth and strategic location.

events.title: Liberia Declares Independence
events.description: Liberia, settled by freed African Americans and formerly enslaved people with the support of the American Colonization Society, declared itself a sovereign nation. Joseph Jenkins Roberts became its first president.
events.significance: Liberia is Africa's oldest modern republic, and its founding remains a complex chapter in the history of the African diaspora.

events.title: The FBI Is Founded
events.description: The U.S. Attorney General ordered the creation of a small corps of special agents within the Department of Justice. It began as the Bureau of Investigation.
events.significance: This small group grew into the Federal Bureau of Investigation, which became the nation's principal federal law enforcement agency.

events.title: The Attack on the Moncada Barracks
events.description: Fidel Castro led a band of rebels in an assault on the Moncada Barracks in Santiago de Cuba. The attack failed militarily, and many of the participants were captured or killed.
events.significance: The date gave its name to Castro's 26th of July Movement, which went on to overthrow the Cuban government in 1959.
